result.rationale: The handler lowercases blacklist entries ('process.env.BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS.split(",").map((email) => email.toLowerCase())') but compares guests with exact '===' against booking.attendees.email and 'blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)' without lowercasing guest, so case-variant emails bypass the blacklist and dedup, creating near-duplicate attendees. Mechanism directly verifiable in addGuests.handler.ts.

judged_text: Case-sensitivity asymmetry defeats the blacklist and dedup checks: blacklist entries are lowercased but guest emails are compared as-typed with exact-match includes and ===, so "Admin@Example.com" bypasses a blacklisted "admin@example.com" and case-variants of existing attendees create near-duplicate guests; the client's Set-based uniqueness is also case-sensitive and won't catch this

record.issue_text: Case-sensitivity asymmetry defeats the blacklist and dedup checks: blacklist entries are lowercased but guest emails are compared as-typed with exact-match includes and ===, so "Admin@Example.com" bypasses a blacklisted "admin@example.com" and case-variants of existing attendees create near-duplicate guests; the client's Set-based uniqueness is also case-sensitive and won't catch this

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `blacklistedGuestEmails` are normalized to lowercase, but incoming `guests` are not (`!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`), so a case-variant like `Admin@Example.com` would not match a blacklist entry `admin@example.com`. Similarly, deduping against existing attendees uses strict equality (`guest === attendee.email`) without normalization, allowing case-variants to be added as near-duplicates. On the client, `Set`-based uniqueness in `AddGuestsDialog` is also case-sensitive, so it won’t prevent such variants either.
